title: Propose-Filter-Release: Scaling Noise to Typical Sensitivity via Private Filtering
why_read: A solid theoretical contribution to differential privacy that generalizes an existing technique for avoiding worst-case noise scaling.
analysis: Differentially private algorithms typically add noise sized to the worst possible single data point's influence, which can make results needlessly noisy when most data is well-behaved. This paper introduces a general method, propose-filter-release, that privately removes atypical records first so the remaining noise can be scaled to the typical case instead. It generalizes a known technique called propose-test-release and shows it applies to several statistical problems, including graph analysis and user histogram comparisons. This is a solid theoretical contribution for the differential privacy community but is fairly specialized and less relevant outside that niche.
